Action Plan:
1. Purchase an oral thermometer today and begin twice-daily temperature checks; document readings.
2. Continue symptomatic relief with Lemsip (contains paracetamol) up to 2–3 sachets/day; avoid any other paracetamol-containing products.
3. Daytime: no cough syrup; Night-time: small amount of cough syrup permitted if cough prevents sleep.
4. Return for review (phone/telehealth or in person) if any of the following occur:
   • Temperature ≥37.5–38 °C persisting or spiking after today  
   • Worsening cough, development of purulent sputum, haemoptysis, chest pain, or shortness of breath  
   • Persistent or worsening green nasal discharge or facial pain suggesting bacterial sinusitis
5. Possible antibiotic therapy will be considered at re-assessment if bacterial infection suspected.
6. Maintain routine diabetes and blood-pressure reviews with GP as previously scheduled.
7. Verbal consent from patient has been obtained before using transcription software.

Subjective:
• Reason for visit: 5-day history of dry cough and continuously streaming nose.  
• History of presenting complaint:  
  – Onset: abrupt, 5 days ago; progression persistent.  
  – Cough: dry, every 20–30 min, no sputum, no haemoptysis, no chest pain, no dyspnoea.  
  – Nasal symptoms: profuse rhinorrhoea described as “pretty green.” No epistaxis or facial pain.  
  – Systemic: feels “hot,” alternating chills; no documented temperature; myalgias present.  
  – Transient diarrhoea at onset; resolved. No vomiting since.  
  – No sore throat, ear pain, headache, visual changes, or rash.  
  – Fluid intake normal; urine output normal.  
• Past medical history: Type 2 diabetes mellitus; hypertension. Denies chronic lung disease.  
• Medications:  
  – Metformin (dose/route/frequency not documented)  
  – Lisinopril (patient reports “200” mg; exact dose not documented)  
  – Lemsip cold remedy PRN (paracetamol-containing; dose per sachet, frequency 2–3/day)  
• Allergies: No known drug allergies; seasonal hay fever only.  
• Social history: Lives with partner and dog; works as office manager; drinks occasional sherry; smoking status not documented.  

Objective:
• Remote consultation—no direct physical examination performed.  
• Patient denies dyspnoea, wheeze, or chest pain. Speech full sentences; no distress observed on video.  
• No vital signs recorded. No current labs or imaging.

Assessment & Plan:

1. Acute cough with rhinorrhoea:
   - Assessment / likely diagnosis: Acute viral upper respiratory tract infection (common cold/influenza-like illness). Supported by DDx item “Acute viral upper respiratory tract infection (High).”
   - Differential diagnosis:  
     • COVID-19 infection (DDx Medium) – no anosmia/ageusia, but clinically possible.  
     • Acute bacterial sinusitis (DDx Medium) – green discharge; monitor for facial pain/fever.  
     • ACE-inhibitor–induced cough (DDx Low) – less likely; does not explain systemic symptoms.  
   - Investigations planned: Home temperature monitoring; none ordered today.  
   - Treatment planned: Symptomatic care with Lemsip; avoid excessive paracetamol. Night-time cough syrup if sleep-disturbing. Hydration, rest.  
   - Safety-net advice: Seek review if fever ≥37.5–38 °C persists/worsens, cough deteriorates, purulent sputum, haemoptysis, chest pain, or breathlessness. Possible antibiotics at that point.

2. Type 2 diabetes mellitus (chronic condition review):
   - Assessment / likely diagnosis: Stable T2DM (recent bloods “normal” 3 weeks ago).  
   - Differential diagnosis: None.  
   - Investigations planned: Routine diabetes blood tests and review per GP schedule.  
   - Treatment planned: Continue metformin; maintain regular monitoring (patient currently lacks home glucometer).  
   - Relevant referrals: None today; continue usual GP follow-up.

3. Hypertension (chronic condition review):
   - Assessment / likely diagnosis: Essential hypertension—control status uncertain (patient unsure of recent BP reading).  
   - Differential diagnosis: None.  
   - Investigations planned: Routine blood-pressure check at next GP visit.  
   - Treatment planned: Continue lisinopril (dose not confirmed).  
   - Relevant referrals: None today.

Quality checks:
● Missing elements: smoking status confirmation; complete medication doses; recent BP and HbA1c values; vital signs; physical examination findings; COVID-19 testing/vaccination status.  
● Internal conflicts: None noted between transcript and DDx.  
● Transcript quality: Clear audio; minimal background noise; occasional incomplete address details.
